holidays.name: National Hole in My Bucket Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the endlessly circular children's song about a leaky bucket. Hum along, then try to fix your own bucket problems without getting stuck in a loop with Henry and Liza.
holidays.origin: The folk song is believed to have German roots dating to the 1700s. It became well known in England and the United States by the 1930s. The National Day Calendar later marked May 30 as a day to celebrate it.
holidays.funFact: The song is a dialogue in which every fix for the bucket depends on another task that can't be done without a working bucket. That makes it one of the most famous catch-22s in folk music.

holidays.name: National Mint Julep Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a frosty silver cup of bourbon, fresh mint, sugar and crushed ice. It's a Southern classic, best sipped slowly on a warm afternoon.
holidays.origin: The mint julep dates to the 18th century in the American South. Kentucky Senator Henry Clay is often credited with popularizing it. As early as 1816, county fair champions in the South were awarded silver julep cups.
holidays.funFact: The mint julep has been the official drink of the Kentucky Derby since 1938.

holidays.name: National Water a Flower Day
holidays.description: A gentle reminder to give your thirsty blooms a drink. It also invites you to tend the garden of a neighbor who is homebound or in the hospital.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance, recognized each year on May 30 as flower gardens approach full bloom.
holidays.funFact: Newly planted seeds often need watering every day until they germinate.
